protected_constraints.rule: Historical use, current deployment, frequency, or previous creative success does not by itself establish Brand DNA. Visual devices, materials, environments, technologies, compositions, interaction patterns, typography implementations, architectural motifs, or campaign mechanisms remain contextual unless explicitly ratified at a higher constitutional level. Prior success creates evidence, not an obligation to repeat.

SkyyRose protects identity, product truth, factual truth, rights, and approved asset integrity while deliberately maintaining broad creative freedom in how those truths are expressed. Creative systems should not seek safety by repeatedly reproducing prior aesthetics. Within resolved constitutional and factual boundaries, they are expected to explore materially different visual, narrative, material, spatial, technological and experiential directions.
Freedom in one domain never overrides a protected constraint in another.

When a visualization, image, photograph, generated image, video, film, commercial, 3D asset, render, advertisement, product scene, virtual experience, interactive experience, ecommerce asset, or other customer-facing creative represents an actual SkyyRose product, that product must be a faithful replica of the authoritative real product. Creative freedom applies to the world around the product, not the identity of the product itself.
Preserve all visually applicable authoritative characteristics including silhouette, proportions, construction, cut, garment geometry, approved colorway, materials as represented, graphics, artwork, logos, placements, dimensions, trims, relevant stitching/construction details, front/back distinctions, and other SKU-specific characteristics supported by authoritative evidence.
Do not improve, reinterpret, stylize, simplify, hallucinate, substitute, recolor, resize graphics, move logos, invent garment details, merge products, or generate an approximation and present it as the real product.
protected_constraints.scope: Any customer-facing creative representing an actual SkyyRose product
interpretation_limits: Zero tolerance for close-enough real-SKU imagery.

Factual/legal/rights: NONE
Protected assets: LOW / governed by asset-use permission
Constitutional identity: LOW

Creative freedom does not automatically decrease as work moves toward release; uncertainty does. Early modes permit unresolved hypotheses, experimental concepts and clearly labeled proposals. As work advances toward customer-facing use, applicable brand, product, factual, rights, technical, accessibility, commerce and approval requirements must progressively resolve into verified truth.
An innovative idea should not be made conventional merely because it reaches production.

Product fidelity cannot intentionally be deferred as unresolved debt into release production. If a real product will appear in final work, the production path must have a credible fidelity-preserving method before full production approval.

Lifecycle:

```text id="iyfytx"
M1 Research
M2 Creative Exploration
M3 Prototype
M4 Candidate / A-B-n
M5 Production
M6 Release Candidate
M7 Release / Publication
M8 Measurement & Learning
M9 Archive / Provenance
```

A prototype may use an obvious non-product placeholder when exact product rendering is not yet possible.

It may not use an inaccurate product representation that could be mistaken for the actual SKU.

Release Candidate requires applicable:

- Constitution PASS
- Product Fidelity PASS
- Factual Claims PASS
- Rights/Approvals PASS
- Channel Requirements PASS
- Creative QA PASS
- Technical QA PASS
- Accessibility PASS where applicable
- Commerce Integrity PASS where applicable
- novelty/saturation recorded
- experiment evidence recorded where applicable

Publication/deployment/ad spend remain separate consequential actions requiring appropriate authority.

protected_constraints.title: Experiment Classes
protected_constraints.rule:
Maintain four distinct experiment types.

### Creative Direction

Question:

> Which conceptual direction or world best expresses the intended meaning?

### Experience

Question:

> Which interaction, navigation, product-discovery, or shopping model creates the strongest customer experience?

### Execution

Question:

> Which composition, copy, edit, format, hook, sequence, framing, or production execution works best?

### Market

Question:

> Which released version best produces the intended customer or business outcome?

Do not collapse these into one generic “A/B test.”

applicable_rules.rule: SkyyRose favors specific, authored, context-rich expression over generic luxury conventions. Minimal, restrained, or abstract executions are valid, but they should remain deliberate and meaningfully connected to the collection, product, brand, place, story, or applicable creative context rather than becoming interchangeable with another luxury label.

Major SkyyRose collections should have a coherent authored narrative context rooted in their underlying meaning, but individual executions do not need to tell the entire story. When narrative devices are used—story, atmosphere, symbolism, place, character, sequence, or environmental interaction—they should serve the collection, product, or meaning rather than exist as disconnected spectacle.

SkyyRose may express collection identity through environments, spatial storytelling, materials, light, place, symbols, character, or other world-building devices when they meaningfully support the collection. The durable principle is intentional, authored contextualization—not a requirement for literal rooms, 3D scenes, monuments, bridges, thrones, or any particular environment.

SkyyRose may separate storytelling from transactional presentation, but the two should remain meaningfully connected. Editorial, cinematic, spatial, symbolic, or environmental experiences should provide an understandable route toward the relevant collection or products when used in a commerce context. Product identity, price, availability, selection, and purchase state remain factual commerce concerns and must not be obscured, fictionalized, or subordinated to storytelling.

SkyyRose treats atmosphere, wonder, emotional impact, and spectacle as legitimate creative purposes. Immersive techniques—including animation, 3D, spatial interaction, cinematic transitions, environmental storytelling, and emerging media—do not need to function solely as transactional utilities. However, experiences introducing substantial complexity, interaction cost, performance cost, or technical overhead should earn that complexity through an intentional role in storytelling, emotional impact, product discovery, exploration, brand experience, or another defined purpose. Technical sophistication alone is insufficient justification.

SkyyRose may use mystery, exploration, unconventional navigation, delayed revelation, or intentional creative friction when those choices meaningfully serve the experience. Creative work does not need to behave like conventional ecommerce. However, users must not become unintentionally trapped, lose essential orientation, or lose access to critical product and commerce actions. Essential controls and appropriate accessibility, preference, device, and capability fallbacks should remain understandable and recoverable.

SkyyRose uses cinematic thinking as a compositional, narrative, and experiential discipline rather than as a mandatory visual effect. Cinematic expression may emerge through framing, sequencing, pacing, scale, tension, reveal, atmosphere, sound, silence, movement, stillness, place, character, product focus, interaction, or spatial experience. No particular grading, darkness, camera movement, film grain, transition style, aspect ratio, 3D technique, or visual effect is inherently required.
SkyyRose should actively explore new forms of fashion shopping, product discovery, storytelling, and interaction that give customers experiences beyond conventional ecommerce patterns. Innovation should create meaningful discovery, emotion, participation, understanding, surprise, or connection between customer, collection, story and product rather than novelty for novelty's sake.
3D rooms, cinematic scrolling, environmental discovery, interactive worlds, spatial commerce, game-like exploration, adaptive storytelling and emerging technologies are creative territories—not permanent templates. Future work should be free to invent materially different shopping experiences when they preserve product truth, brand identity, recoverable control, accessibility and commerce integrity.
A still, bright, minimal, physical, conversational, spatial, playful, documentary, photographic, or yet-uninvented experience may be as authentically SkyyRose as today's animated cinematic environments when it carries intentional direction, authored meaning and compelling customer experience.

SkyyRose is expected to evolve creatively rather than repeatedly reproduce previously successful executions. Major campaigns, collection experiences, and significant creative initiatives should introduce materially new creative territory through one or more dimensions such as visual direction, materials, environments, storytelling mechanisms, interaction models, media, technology, composition, product discovery, or shopping experience.
Innovation may combine multiple dimensions when the result is coherent. Existing motifs, technologies, materials, environments, or interaction patterns may be reused when contextually meaningful, but previous success alone is insufficient justification for repetition.
SkyyRose should not optimize itself into sameness. Historical repetition and short-term performance are evidence, not permanent creative boundaries. Performance evidence may inform future decisions but may not automatically redefine Brand DNA, eliminate meaningful experimentation, or permanently narrow creative territory.

Historical use, current deployment, frequency, or previous creative success does not by itself establish Brand DNA. Visual devices, materials, environments, technologies, compositions, interaction patterns, typography implementations, architectural motifs, or campaign mechanisms remain contextual unless explicitly ratified at a higher constitutional level. Prior success creates evidence, not an obligation to repeat.

Protected asset treatments remain protected where applicable; environmental materials may evolve.

Current exact typography implementation.

`typography.json` remains authoritative for the existing storefront until intentionally changed, but today's fonts are not eternal Brand DNA.

Current hero composition, centered emblem, oversized wordmark, character placement, product-grid structure, or world→product sequence.

Preserve underlying grammar, not composition formulas.

---

Oakland and the broader Bay Area are important creative territories that future systems should actively consider when place, geography, architecture, infrastructure, culture, movement, landscape, or local storytelling can meaningfully strengthen the work.
Creative systems should look beyond previously used landmarks and investigate relevant Bay Area-specific features, architecture, bridges, streets, neighborhoods, landscapes, transit forms, industrial environments, waterfronts, cultural locations, natural geography, and other locally grounded visual or narrative material when appropriate.
No individual bridge, skyline, landmark, neighborhood or location becomes mandatory through repetition. Bay Area specificity should expand creative territory rather than collapse it into repeated Bay Bridge, Golden Gate or skyline imagery.
Geographic references must remain truthful and may not rewrite origin, product story, partnership status or historical meaning.
applicable_rules.scope: Local discovery when place meaningfully strengthens the work

applicable_rules.rule:
SkyyRose protects identity, product truth, factual truth, rights, and approved asset integrity while deliberately maintaining broad creative freedom in how those truths are expressed. Creative systems should not seek safety by repeatedly reproducing prior aesthetics. Within resolved constitutional and factual boundaries, they are expected to explore materially different visual, narrative, material, spatial, technological and experiential directions.
Freedom in one domain never overrides a protected constraint in another.

When a visualization, image, photograph, generated image, video, film, commercial, 3D asset, render, advertisement, product scene, virtual experience, interactive experience, ecommerce asset, or other customer-facing creative represents an actual SkyyRose product, that product must be a faithful replica of the authoritative real product. Creative freedom applies to the world around the product, not the identity of the product itself.
Preserve all visually applicable authoritative characteristics including silhouette, proportions, construction, cut, garment geometry, approved colorway, materials as represented, graphics, artwork, logos, placements, dimensions, trims, relevant stitching/construction details, front/back distinctions, and other SKU-specific characteristics supported by authoritative evidence.
Do not improve, reinterpret, stylize, simplify, hallucinate, substitute, recolor, resize graphics, move logos, invent garment details, merge products, or generate an approximation and present it as the real product.
applicable_rules.scope: Any customer-facing creative representing an actual SkyyRose product
interpretation_limits: Zero tolerance for close-enough real-SKU imagery.

applicable_rules.rule:
Establish:

```text id="0dsh4p"
EXACT_PRODUCT
Real SKU represented.
Strict fidelity gate.

PRODUCT_CONCEPT
Proposal / nonexistent or future product.
Must be clearly labeled internally.
Cannot masquerade as existing product truth.

BRAND_ABSTRACT
No real product represented.
Broad creative freedom.
```

If authoritative evidence is insufficient for an exact required view:

**BLOCKED — insufficient authoritative product evidence.**

Do not invent the missing view.

---
applicable_rules.scope: Product representation mode and required evidence

applicable_rules.rule: When unconstrained regeneration cannot reliably preserve exact product fidelity, prefer fidelity-preserving production techniques such as approved source photography, compositing, validated product photography, validated 3D assets, product scans, controlled rendering, or another method capable of preserving the real product.

Specify as a non-bypassable future Creative OS verification stage:

```text id="3by3wl"
Resolve SKU
    ↓
get_product(sku)
    ↓
Resolve required authoritative views
    ↓
Load authoritative references
    ↓
Produce / composite / render
    ↓
PRODUCT FIDELITY GATE
    │
    ├── silhouette
    ├── proportions
    ├── construction
    ├── colorway
    ├── artwork
    ├── logo
    ├── placement
    ├── material appearance
    ├── front/back
    └── relevant detail
    ↓
PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED
```

FAIL requires remediation.

BLOCKED prevents release-ready status.

---
Factual/legal/rights: NONE
Protected assets: LOW / governed by asset-use permission
Constitutional identity: LOW
Voice: MODERATE
Typography: MODERATE, subject to applicable current implementation authority
Motion: HIGH
Composition: HIGH
Materials/lighting: HIGH
Environment/place: HIGH
Campaign story/metaphor: HIGH
Shopping/interaction model: HIGH
New concepts: OPEN at proposal stage
Cross-domain synthesis: HIGH when ideas form a coherent concept rather than feature stacking
Material exploration should actively move beyond repeatedly defaulting to chrome/marble/black when the applicable context permits.
applicable_rules.scope: Environmental material exploration; protected product and asset constraints remain binding

applicable_rules.rule:
Creative freedom does not automatically decrease as work moves toward release; uncertainty does. Early modes permit unresolved hypotheses, experimental concepts and clearly labeled proposals. As work advances toward customer-facing use, applicable brand, product, factual, rights, technical, accessibility, commerce and approval requirements must progressively resolve into verified truth.
An innovative idea should not be made conventional merely because it reaches production.

Product fidelity cannot intentionally be deferred as unresolved debt into release production. If a real product will appear in final work, the production path must have a credible fidelity-preserving method before full production approval.

Lifecycle:

```text id="iyfytx"
M1 Research
M2 Creative Exploration
M3 Prototype
M4 Candidate / A-B-n
M5 Production
M6 Release Candidate
M7 Release / Publication
M8 Measurement & Learning
M9 Archive / Provenance
```

A prototype may use an obvious non-product placeholder when exact product rendering is not yet possible.

It may not use an inaccurate product representation that could be mistaken for the actual SKU.

Release Candidate requires applicable:

- Constitution PASS
- Product Fidelity PASS
- Factual Claims PASS
- Rights/Approvals PASS
- Channel Requirements PASS
- Creative QA PASS
- Technical QA PASS
- Accessibility PASS where applicable
- Commerce Integrity PASS where applicable
- novelty/saturation recorded
- experiment evidence recorded where applicable

Publication/deployment/ad spend remain separate consequential actions requiring appropriate authority.

applicable_rules.title: Heir / Next Generation
applicable_rules.rule: Kids Capsule expresses heir, continuation, inheritance, imagination, possibility, and the next generation of SkyyRose. These underlying ideas are durable Kids context. Specific devices such as the current throne, royal room, mascot treatment, procession, playroom, character style, or individual scene are creative expressions rather than permanent constitutional requirements.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Kids Capsule expresses heir, continuation, inheritance, imagination, possibility, and the next generation of SkyyRose. These underlying ideas are durable Kids context. Specific devices such as the current throne, royal room, mascot treatment, procession, playroom, character style, or individual scene are creative expressions rather than permanent constitutional requirements.**

This is the durable meaning.

Do not reduce Kids to:

> throne + gold room + mascot

Future Kids worlds may look materially different while remaining faithful to heir / continuation / next-generation meaning.

applicable_rules.title: Independent Creative Language
applicable_rules.rule:
Kids may develop a materially distinct creative language from the adult SkyyRose collections. It may be more playful, colorful, imaginative, character-driven, tactile, game-like, exploratory, fantastical, interactive, surprising, or technologically experimental while remaining connected to the master Brand Constitution.

Kids should not simply be adult SkyyRose made smaller.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Kids may develop a materially distinct creative language from the adult SkyyRose collections. It may be more playful, colorful, imaginative, character-driven, tactile, game-like, exploratory, fantastical, interactive, surprising, or technologically experimental while remaining connected to the master Brand Constitution.**

Hard rule:

> **Kids should not simply be adult SkyyRose made smaller.**

The system should treat Kids as its own contextual world, not as a scaled-down version of Black Rose, Love Hurts, or Signature.

applicable_rules.title: Kids as Experiential Innovation Territory
applicable_rules.rule: Kids is a priority territory for exploring new forms of shopping, product discovery, play, storytelling, interaction, character agency, spatial experience, physical/digital combinations, game mechanics, adaptive journeys, and emerging technologies when those approaches are appropriate to the job.

applicable_rules.title: Kids Product Fidelity
applicable_rules.rule: Creative freedom around Kids never reduces product fidelity requirements. Any actual SkyyRose Kids Capsule product represented visually must remain an exact, verifiable representation of the real product.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Creative freedom around Kids never reduces product fidelity requirements. Any actual SkyyRose Kids Capsule product represented visually must remain an exact, verifiable representation of the real product.**

The Kids world may be fantastical.

The garment may not be fictionalized.

applicable_rules.title: Character and World Separation
applicable_rules.rule: Characters, mascots, rooms, environments, and narrative objects belong to contextual creative expression unless separately ratified. Their existence does not grant authority to redesign products, logos, collection marks, origin history, or other protected truth.
applicable_rules.source_context:
Recommended additional rule:

> **Characters, mascots, rooms, environments, and narrative objects belong to contextual creative expression unless separately ratified. Their existence does not grant authority to redesign products, logos, collection marks, origin history, or other protected truth.**

This prevents a powerful character/world system from slowly becoming the authority for the whole brand.

applicable_rules.title: Color Authority Is Domain-Specific
applicable_rules.rule: SkyyRose does not use one universal color authority for every visual domain. Product color, protected brand/collection asset color, interface color, environmental color, photographic color, campaign palette, lighting color, and natural-location color are separate scopes.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **SkyyRose does not use one universal color authority for every visual domain. Product color, protected brand/collection asset color, interface color, environmental color, photographic color, campaign palette, lighting color, and natural-location color are separate scopes.**

Never infer permission across those scopes automatically.

applicable_rules.title: Product Color Is Locked
applicable_rules.rule: Actual SkyyRose product colorways must reproduce the authoritative real product exactly. Campaign palette, lighting, environmental art direction, interface colors, or atmospheric effects may not silently recolor the product.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Actual SkyyRose product colorways must reproduce the authoritative real product exactly. Campaign palette, lighting, environmental art direction, interface colors, or atmospheric effects may not silently recolor the product.**

Example:

```text
Blue sky                 allowed
Blue environmental light context-dependent
Blue interface status    allowed when appropriate

Actual black garment
rendered as blue          NOT allowed
```

The Exact Product Fidelity Gate remains controlling.

applicable_rules.title: Protected Marks and Artwork
applicable_rules.rule: Approved logos, collection marks, artwork, garment graphics, and protected assets retain their governed color and material treatments where applicable. Environmental palette freedom does not automatically authorize recoloring protected marks.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Approved logos, collection marks, artwork, garment graphics, and protected assets retain their governed color and material treatments where applicable. Environmental palette freedom does not automatically authorize recoloring protected marks.**

Asset permissions remain scoped by actual approval.

applicable_rules.title: Environmental and Campaign Palette Freedom
applicable_rules.rule: Environmental, editorial, cinematic, and campaign palettes may explore broadly—including palettes outside historically dominant dark, black, metallic, crimson, gold, silver, or rose-gold treatments—when the palette meaningfully supports the collection, concept, location, material system, narrative, channel, or experience.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Environmental, editorial, cinematic, and campaign palettes may explore broadly—including palettes outside historically dominant dark, black, metallic, crimson, gold, silver, or rose-gold treatments—when the palette meaningfully supports the collection, concept, location, material system, narrative, channel, or experience.**

This is important for creative evolution.

The Creative OS should not default to:

> black + chrome + dramatic red/gold

simply because those treatments dominate recent work.

applicable_rules.title: Natural Color Is Not Brand Recoloring
applicable_rules.rule: Truthful natural colors appearing through skies, water, vegetation, architecture, streets, people, materials, documentary photography, Bay Area locations, or other real-world environments do not automatically establish or violate a master-brand palette rule.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Truthful natural colors appearing through skies, water, vegetation, architecture, streets, people, materials, documentary photography, Bay Area locations, or other real-world environments do not automatically establish or violate a master-brand palette rule.**

This directly protects the Bay Area discovery principle.

A blue-gray sky does not mean:

> blue is now a master SkyyRose brand color.

Likewise, a historical ban cannot automatically erase truthful natural color from a location.

applicable_rules.title: Accessible Interface Color
applicable_rules.rule: Interface colors may adapt as necessary for accessibility, contrast, semantic state, readability, interaction feedback, and usability without redefining product color or master-brand identity.
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Interface colors may adapt as necessary for accessibility, contrast, semantic state, readability, interaction feedback, and usability without redefining product color or master-brand identity.**

UI red, blue, green, warning yellow, focus rings, and similar semantic colors should not accidentally become apparel or campaign authority.

applicable_rules.title: Palette as Innovation Dimension
applicable_rules.rule: Palette may itself be a deliberate dimension of creative evolution. Major campaigns should not be forced into historically dominant dark or metallic treatments solely for recognition.

applicable_rules.title: Palette Provenance
applicable_rules.rule: When a palette is materially consequential to a campaign or collection, record whether its authority comes from product truth, protected brand assets, collection context, campaign art direction, environment, accessibility requirements, or creative proposal.
applicable_rules.source_context:
Recommended addition:

> **When a palette is materially consequential to a campaign or collection, record whether its authority comes from product truth, protected brand assets, collection context, campaign art direction, environment, accessibility requirements, or creative proposal.**

This makes future conflicts much easier to resolve.

applicable_rules.title: Creative Saturation Awareness
applicable_rules.rule: Before major creative production, review recent and relevant SkyyRose work for repeated visual devices, materials, environments, locations, compositions, motifs, technologies, narrative structures, camera languages, interactions, shopping mechanics, and campaign patterns.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Before major creative production, review recent and relevant SkyyRose work for repeated visual devices, materials, environments, locations, compositions, motifs, technologies, narrative structures, camera languages, interactions, shopping mechanics, and campaign patterns.**

This is awareness, not prohibition.

The purpose is to know when repetition is intentional versus automatic.

applicable_rules.title: Material Novelty Requirement
applicable_rules.rule: Major campaigns, collection experiences, commercials, short films, significant web experiences, and other major creative initiatives should introduce materially new creative territory through one or more meaningful dimensions.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Major campaigns, collection experiences, commercials, short films, significant web experiences, and other major creative initiatives should introduce materially new creative territory through one or more meaningful dimensions.**

Novelty dimensions may include:

```text
visual direction
material language
palette
environment
location
architecture
composition
camera language
story structure
character
sound
media
motion
technology
interaction
product discovery
shopping mechanic
physical/digital relationship
channel behavior
```

Multiple dimensions may be combined.

applicable_rules.title: Difference Must Be Meaningful
applicable_rules.rule: Novelty cannot be satisfied by cosmetic variation alone. The creative system must be able to state what is materially different from recent work and why that difference matters to the intended customer, collection, narrative, shopping experience, or campaign objective.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning

applicable_rules.title: Creative A/B/n Hypotheses
applicable_rules.rule: Major creative initiatives should explore multiple materially distinct hypotheses before expensive final production when practical.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning

applicable_rules.title: Experiment Classes
applicable_rules.rule:
Maintain four distinct experiment types.

### Creative Direction

Question:

> Which conceptual direction or world best expresses the intended meaning?

### Experience

Question:

> Which interaction, navigation, product-discovery, or shopping model creates the strongest customer experience?

### Execution

Question:

> Which composition, copy, edit, format, hook, sequence, framing, or production execution works best?

### Market

Question:

> Which released version best produces the intended customer or business outcome?

Do not collapse these into one generic “A/B test.”
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
Maintain four distinct experiment types.

### Creative Direction

Question:

> Which conceptual direction or world best expresses the intended meaning?

### Experience

Question:

### Execution

Question:

### Market

Question:

> Which released version best produces the intended customer or business outcome?

Do not collapse these into one generic “A/B test.”

applicable_rules.title: Synthesis Is Allowed
applicable_rules.rule: Experimentation is not winner-takes-all. Strong elements from multiple directions may be deliberately combined when their synthesis produces a coherent concept stronger than the individual candidates.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Experimentation is not winner-takes-all. Strong elements from multiple directions may be deliberately combined when their synthesis produces a coherent concept stronger than the individual candidates.**

Example:

```text
A
strongest material system

B
strongest narrative

C
strongest shopping mechanic

        ↓

D
A materials
+
B narrative
+
C interaction

        ↓

new prototype
```

The synthesis must itself be tested.

Do not feature-stack unrelated ideas merely to appear innovative.

applicable_rules.title: Performance Does Not Rewrite Brand DNA
applicable_rules.rule: Advertising, engagement, conversion, commerce, audience, or creative performance may inform future execution, channel strategy, and hypothesis selection, but performance alone may not automatically redefine Brand Constitution, product truth, or permanent creative boundaries.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Advertising, engagement, conversion, commerce, audience, or creative performance may inform future execution, channel strategy, and hypothesis selection, but performance alone may not automatically redefine Brand Constitution, product truth, or permanent creative boundaries.**

A high-performing generic execution means:

> it performed well in that tested context.

It does not mean:

> generic execution is now SkyyRose identity.

applicable_rules.title: Never Optimize Into Sameness
applicable_rules.rule: SkyyRose must not optimize itself into creative sameness. Historical success, recent creative similarity, and short-term performance are evidence rather than permanent creative limits. Future work should continue testing materially new territory.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **SkyyRose must not optimize itself into creative sameness. Historical success, recent creative similarity, and short-term performance are evidence rather than permanent creative limits. Future work should continue testing materially new territory.**

The system should optimize:

```text
RECOGNIZABLE IDENTITY
        +
MEANINGFUL NOVELTY
        +
CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE
        +
PRODUCT TRUTH
```

not simply visual similarity to previous campaigns.

applicable_rules.title: Novelty and Brand Compliance Are Independent Axes
applicable_rules.rule: A creative direction should be evaluated separately for constitutional compliance and meaningful novelty. High similarity to prior SkyyRose work is not proof of brand correctness, and high novelty is not proof of brand violation.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
Recommended hard rule:

> **A creative direction should be evaluated separately for constitutional compliance and meaningful novelty. High similarity to prior SkyyRose work is not proof of brand correctness, and high novelty is not proof of brand violation.**

Conceptually:

```text
                NOVELTY
                  ↑
                  │
       innovative │ innovative
       but wrong  │ + on-brand
                  │
─────────────── BRAND COMPLIANCE ───────→
                  │
       repetitive │ familiar
       + wrong    │ + on-brand
                  │
```

Desired major creative work generally aims toward:

> **on-brand + materially new**

applicable_rules.title: Creative Difference Map
applicable_rules.rule:
For major concepts, record a concise difference map against relevant recent work.

Example:

```text
environment       NEW
materials         NEW
palette           EVOLVED
interaction       NEW
story structure   NEW
camera language   EXISTING
typography        EXISTING
product framing   EXISTING
shopping model    NEW
```

If nearly every material dimension is unchanged, the system should challenge whether the direction genuinely satisfies Creative Evolution.

```text
failures
saturation update
```

applicable_rules.rule: Campaign and experiment learning belongs to contextual knowledge unless explicitly ratified into the Constitution by the owner.
applicable_rules.scope: Creative saturation, novelty, experimentation and contextual learning
applicable_rules.source_context:
> **Campaign and experiment learning belongs to contextual knowledge unless explicitly ratified into the Constitution by the owner.**

The learning loop is:

```text
CREATE
  ↓
TEST
  ↓
LEARN
  ↓
CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE
```

```text
CREATE
```
